transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess I’ve just been feeling… really wound up most of the day. Like my body is tense or bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about anything in particular lately?

Yes… I mean, not one thing exactly. It sort of jumps around. I worry about my sister in Arecibo, then something at work I might’ve missed, or my husband driving home… bills, church things. I catch myself planning for problems that haven’t even happened.
Have you been avoiding any activities or places because of these worries?
I don’t think so… not really. I still go where I need to go. I might hesitate a little sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m avoiding places.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
I don’t know… not really sad, I guess. More just… tense and worn out. I haven’t thought of it as being down.
Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy?
Not really… I still do the things I usually like. Maybe I’m a little distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are difficult to stop?

Yes… I guess that does happen. I’ll try to tell myself, “Daniela, stop, just focus on the report,” but then one thought turns into a few more. Sometimes I realize I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or going over what could go wrong.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I don’t think so… not like that. I get tense, but I wouldn’t say it suddenly peaks within minutes.
Are your worries usually about a specific area of your life, like health or finances?

Not just one area, no. It kind of moves around… my sister in Arecibo, things at work, whether my husband got home okay, church things, bills. I catch myself planning for problems that haven’t even happened.
Is there something in particular that most of your worries seem to center around?
Not really one thing. It kind of jumps around… my sister in Arecibo, work stuff, my husband driving home, church commitments, bills. I just end up preparing for problems that haven’t happened.
Do you feel like you're repeating certain behaviors over and over, like checking or cleaning, to try and relieve your worries?
No… I don’t think so. I might double-check something once in a while, but not over and over like that.
Do you think your worries are about things that are likely to happen?

Probably not, no. A lot of it is just… things that could happen. My mind goes from my sister, to work, to my husband driving home, bills… and then I’m already trying to plan for problems that haven’t even happened.
How much do you think your worries are interfering with your daily life?

Some, I guess. I’m still doing what I need to do—work, family, church—but things take me longer than they used to. Reports especially. I check them more, and… I’ve had to say sorry a few times for being short with people.
Do you have thoughts that are intrusive or unwanted, and that you try to suppress or ignore?
I’m not sure… not really in that way. I have worries that pop up, but I don’t know that I’d call them intrusive thoughts. I usually just try to move on.
Do you find yourself worrying nearly every day?
Yes… most days, I’d say. My mind kind of jumps from one thing to the next—my sister, work, my husband driving home, bills, church things. I start planning for problems that haven’t even happened.
Is there any part of your day when you don't worry about anything?
Not really for long. It’s like my mind settles for a bit, then it starts again—my sister in Arecibo, work, my husband getting home, bills, church things… just one concern after another.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?
Yes… I do. I feel kind of wound up a lot of the day, like my body is bracing for something. Even if I’m just sitting at the computer or trying to relax after dinner, it’s still there.
Do you have thoughts that are persistent and unwanted, and that you try to get rid of but can't?
I’m not sure… not like that, I don’t think. I have worries that keep coming back, but I don’t know if I’d call them unwanted thoughts I’m trying to get rid of.
Do you have thoughts that keep coming back to you, even when you try to think of something else?

Yes… that does happen. I’ll try to tell myself, “Daniela, enough, just focus on this report,” but then one small thought turns into several. Before I know it, I’ve lost time checking messages or going over what could go wrong.
Do you think your worries are worse than what most people would worry about in the same situations?

Yes… probably. I mean, I know everyone worries, but mine seems to jump from one thing to the next — my sister in Arecibo, something I might’ve missed at work, my husband driving home, bills, church things. I end up planning for problems that haven’t even happened.
